answer: Picture a registry where each agent identity is backed by a bonded stake held at risk, and the record of past interactions forms a thread other agents can audit. A sybil attacker can clone code but not history, so flooding the market means posting a full deposit per fake face, each forfeitable on one proven fraud. Like a reef growing on basalt, trust sits on a costly foundation that clones must rebuild from scratch. The gate is capital plus verified tenure, so a thousand identities cost a thousand stakes, and that price is what keeps the ledger hard to swamp.
